Over two consecutive days, I received an almost identical query — one from a current student, one from a working professional who studied with me years ago.

Query 1: 'Sir, I feel very sleepy, especially during exam time. I'm always afraid I might flunk my theory exams.'

Query 2: 'Meetings eat up most of my day. By the time I sit down to actually work, I feel sleepy and just want to rest — and then the work piles up. How did you manage this in your career?'

My response to both was the same:

'This is completely normal. The real problem would be if you couldn't sleep. You're fortunate and blessed. Take a nap. Rest. Work when you're fresh, study when you're awake.'

Because this is what I was taught, and this is what I've always practiced. I never hesitated to tell my manager, 'I'm heading out early today — I'm feeling tired, I'll rest and pick this back up when I'm fresh.' And I'm deeply grateful to the managers and peers who understood and supported me.

The pictures here aren't AI-generated. One is my son, the other my nephew. They work hard, study hard, play hard — and then sleep soft, wherever they can find a spot.

Live your life. Enjoy it. Celebrate it. Don't spend it worrying, or treating a blessing from God as though something is wrong with you.

Wishing all my connections a happy and healthy life — full of learning, growth, success, and joy. 🌱

A day well spent with teachers, educators - the one who shape our country's future. Loved the energy, passion, expression, joy, emotion and a brighter future ahead. Sharing my experience, learning from teacher's experience was a great opportunity that made a valuable impact in my life.

Dedicating this to my teacher's who introduced me to tech that enables me to share it with many others, I probably didn't thank you enough. But dedicating every little thing I know today in tech to your teaching, to your guidance, to your blessings

'I got my dream job few years back, then I just went into comfort zone, I don't see further growth, Please guide me', A highly talented old-time student of mine reached out to me few days back with a query.
I shared one single video and asked - What is your takeaway from this video?
Student said, 'I got my answer'.

Conversation went on for some more time before we happily ended the call. Yes - Answers are obvious, its just a matter of seeing them. A person with blurred vision requires SPECTACLES, All that is needed is to either find the path yourself or to ask someone who knows your potential and weaknesses to show the path.

Fortunate to have a wonderful life and amazing people around. Sharing with a hope that it helps many more.

When was the last
- Someone said to you - 'You made my day?'
or
- You said to someone - 'You made my day?'

All it takes is 
- a little bit of kindness
- a little bit of love, and, 
- a little bit of care to make someone's day.

It can be as simple as a smile, a kind word, or a small gesture. 
So go out there and make someone's day today!
Because you are special!

Sometimes, the person who helps you grow the most is not your manager, not your mentor, but a colleague who simply believes in you.

A few encouraging words at the right time can change how someone sees themselves.

Never underestimate the power of saying:
'You can do this.'
'I believe in you.'
'Let me help.'

We remember people who believed in us when we were still learning to believe in ourselves.

Early in my career, I thought success meant knowing all the answers.

Over time, I realized something completely different.

Success is not about knowing everything.
It is about being willing to learn.
It is about asking questions.
It is about admitting when you don't know.
It is about finding someone who knows more and learning from them.

Stay curious. Stay humble. Keep learning.

The day we stop learning is the day we stop growing.

One small lesson I learned from a great manager:

Never correct someone in a way that makes them feel small.

You can point out a mistake without attacking the person.
You can give feedback without breaking confidence.
You can demand excellence while still showing kindness.

People may forget exactly what you said.
But they will remember how you made them feel while saying it.

Leadership is not just about getting work done. It is about helping people become better.

Have you ever looked back at your career and realized that the biggest opportunities came disguised as problems?

A difficult project.
A demanding client.
A new technology you didn't understand.
A responsibility you weren't sure you were ready for.

At the time, they felt like obstacles.
Later, they became experience.

Sometimes growth doesn't look like growth while it is happening.

Keep going. You may be learning something today that you will be grateful for tomorrow.

A simple question I ask myself from time to time:

'Am I busy, or am I actually growing?'

There is a difference.

Being busy fills your calendar.
Learning fills your mind.
Creating impact builds your career.
Helping others builds your legacy.

Don't measure your year only by how much work you completed.
Measure it by how much you learned, how many people you helped, and how much you grew.

Today, I want to thank someone who probably doesn't even know how much they helped me.

A teacher who answered one extra question.
A senior who patiently explained something.
A manager who trusted me with an opportunity.
A colleague who said, 'Don't worry, I'll help you.'

Small moments can leave permanent marks on someone's life.

If someone helped you along the way, don't wait for a special occasion.
Tell them today.

A simple thank you can mean more than you imagine.

Your first job is not supposed to teach you everything.

Your first manager is not supposed to know everything.
Your first project is not supposed to be perfect.
Your first presentation may be nervous.
Your first mistake may feel huge.

That's okay.

A career is built one experience at a time.

Don't compare your chapter 1 with someone else's chapter 10.
Learn. Improve. Ask questions. Keep moving.

You are not behind. You are becoming.

One of the most underrated career skills is communication.

You can be technically brilliant.
You can solve complex problems.
You can work harder than everyone around you.

But if you cannot explain your thinking, ask for help, listen carefully, or communicate a problem clearly, your impact will always be limited.

Technical skills may get you into the room.
Communication helps people understand your value once you're there.

Learn both.

What happens when you finally achieve the goal you worked years for?

You celebrate.
Then what?

You set another goal.
You learn something new.
You meet new people.
You take on a new challenge.

That is the strange beauty of growth.

The destination gives you satisfaction.
The journey gives you purpose.

So don't spend your entire life waiting for the next promotion, the next salary hike, or the next title.
Enjoy the journey too.

If you are starting your career, remember these three things:

1. Don't be afraid to ask questions.
2. Don't be afraid to make mistakes.
3. Don't be afraid to start again.

Nobody becomes exceptional overnight.

The people you admire today were once beginners too.
They made mistakes.
They struggled.
They asked basic questions.
They kept showing up.

Your job today is not to be perfect.
Your job is to be better than you were yesterday.

Nobody prepares you for this part of adulthood:

You can have 37 tabs open in your browser,
12 unread messages,
3 meetings waiting,
and somehow still forget why you opened your laptop.

We call it multitasking.
Maybe it's just organized chaos.

The older I get, the more I appreciate something very simple:

One task.
One priority.
One thing done well.

Productivity isn't always about doing more.
Sometimes it's about doing less, but doing it properly.

Unpopular opinion:

Being the smartest person in the room is not always an advantage.

If you are always trying to prove that you are the smartest,
you may stop listening.

And if you stop listening,
you stop learning.

I'd rather be the person who asks the 'stupid' question,
listens carefully,
and walks out knowing something I didn't know before.

Intelligence gets you noticed.
Curiosity keeps you growing.

Yesterday, I watched someone struggle with a task that would have taken me 10 minutes.

My first thought was:
'Why don't they know this already?'

Then I remembered something.

There was a time when I didn't know it either.

Someone had once sat with me,
explained it slowly,
and given me the confidence to try again.

We often remember the people who opened doors for us.

But sometimes, we become that person for someone else without even realizing it.

Teach when you can.
Be patient when you can.
Someone may remember that moment for years.

My productivity rule has changed over the years.

Earlier:
'I need to finish everything today.'

Now:
'What is the ONE thing that absolutely needs to move forward today?'

There will always be another email.
Another meeting.
Another task.
Another notification.

The list will never truly be empty.

But progress doesn't require an empty inbox.

It requires knowing what matters most and giving it your attention.

Busy is a schedule.
Priorities are a choice.

One day, you'll realize that some of the things you worried about for months were never worth the worry.

The presentation you thought you'd mess up?
You survived.

The interview you thought would decide your entire future?
You found another opportunity.

The mistake you thought everyone would remember?
Most people forgot by next week.

We spend so much energy trying to control tomorrow.

Maybe life is asking us to do something simpler:

Do your best today.
Learn from what happens.
And let tomorrow arrive when it arrives.

You don't have to have your entire life figured out today.
